result.reasoning:
I could not refute the mechanism: the crash is real, and I reproduced the exact erroneous output described (an exception where the kernel's own gate `n > 1` specifies NaN). But my reachability work says the blast radius is much smaller than "medium", and it changes no number in any study.

WHAT IS TRUE (reproduced)
1. Kernel level, /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/partura/ops_ext.py:373: `day_flat_run_max(torch.tensor([[[5.0]]]))` and `day_flat_run_max(torch.zeros((2,2,0)))` both raise `IndexError: max(): Expected reduction dim 2 to have non-zero size.` M>=2 is fine (M=2 returns 0.5 on a flat pair).
2. Pipeline level (this is the part the report did not establish): the crash survives the real path. `partura.panels.parse_research("day_flat_run_max(day_mean(Close))")` parses (the research relaxation in /Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube/src/alphacube/expression.py:144-162 lets a `day_*` reducer take a width-1 operand), `_align_widths` keeps the operand at width 1 (/Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube/src/alphacube/engine/kernels.py:123-142 broadcasts to `max(widths)`, which is 1 for a unary op), and the kernel then sees M=1. On a synthetic 6x12x241 store, `CubeEngine(view).evaluate([...], tolerant=False)` raises `IndexError` for the whole batch. The sibling `day_flat_ratio(day_mean(Close))` returns an all-NaN panel on the same input, so the inconsistency the report describes is real for that sibling.

WHY IT CHANGES NO NUMBER (the part that should downgrade it)
3. Unreachable from mining/selection. The strict search grammar rejects it at construction: `parse("day_flat_run_max(day_mean(Close))")` -> `ParseError: ... needs genuine per-minute variation, got collapsed operand`. GP/RL/boosting/env all build strict trees, the store is always n_minutes=241, and the engine never chunks the minute axis (/Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube/src/alphacube/axes.py: M-axis operators chunk over S or D only). So no mined factor, no 10%-long-book excess, no holdout number can be affected.
4. No such expression exists. I grepped every .py/.yaml/.json/.md in both repos: all ~20 uses are `day_flat_run_max(<field>)` on the full minute axis (studies/F102..F109 hypo*.yaml, research/alpha_distillation/*, guidance/*). Nothing anywhere feeds a day_* operator a collapsed operand; `day_std(day_mean(Close))` appears only as a *negative* case in AlphaCube/tests/test_expression.py:31.
5. Every real caller is tolerant. partura/panels.py:292/303/319 always passes `tolerant=True`, as do research.py, calculate.py, mining/{gp,env,boosting}.py and every script. In that mode the failing node is recorded in `res.errors[i]` ("day_flat_run_max: IndexError: ...") and I verified the other expressions in the same batch come back byte-identical to running them alone. The only `tolerant=False` callers evaluate fixed internal expressions (daily.py:129, scripts/check_store.py:42) that can never contain this operator.
6. Correct behaviour would be an all-NaN panel, i.e. a factor with zero coverage that is discarded anyway. So the real-world difference is "a meaningless hand-written expression fails loudly with a confusing IndexError instead of returning an empty panel". Worth a one-line fix, not a number-changing defect.

ONE CLAIM IN THE REPORT IS WRONG: "every sibling day_* operator degrades gracefully to NaN". `day_pos_ratio(torch.tensor([[[5.0]]]))` returns 1.0, not NaN, at M=1. day_flat_ratio/at_max_ratio/at_min_ratio/distinct_ratio do return NaN. So the proposed "house rule" is not already uniform in the file.

The probes and the catalog never hit this: alphacube/catalog.py `_sample` smoke-tests at (7,5), partura/probes.py runs at (40,24)/(1,401)/(1,2001) — all M>=2, so registration and `signature()`/`neighbours()` in partura/propose.py are unaffected.

result.corrected_fix:
The reported fix (an early-return guard) works but is more code than needed and only special-cases the boundary. Prefer padding the reduction so the final `.max` always has at least one element — `c - reset` is provably >= 0 everywhere (c is a cumsum of 0/1 and `reset` is a cummax of values drawn from earlier c's, so reset <= c), therefore prepending a zero column cannot change the result for any M >= 2. In /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/partura/ops_ext.py, replace line 373

    run = (c - reset).max(dim=-1).values

with

    z = torch.zeros(x.shape[:-1] + (1,), dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device)
    run = torch.cat([z, c - reset], dim=-1).max(dim=-1).values

The existing `n > 1` gate in `_day` then turns M<2 into NaN by itself (verified: M=0 and M=1 both return NaN, and 3600 random panels at M in {241,60,7,3,2} are bit-identical to the current kernel). Keep it after `x = _f(x)` (line 368) so `x.dtype` is floating — a guard placed before `_f` would hand `_day` an integer tensor and `torch.full_like(v, NAN)` would then fail.

Do NOT generalise this into a house rule shared with the separately reported `cs_robust_z` / zero-length-stock-axis case: a zero-length minute axis means "no minutes to compare", which this operator's own docstring already defines as NaN, whereas a zero-length stock axis is an empty universe and should stay an error rather than be silently padded.

Priority: cosmetic/robustness, not number-changing. No expression in either repo can reach it, the strict search grammar forbids it by construction, and every real caller evaluates with tolerant=True, where the failure is confined to the one offending expression.
